newsitem.title: USA: Gynecare says FDA panel to review therapy.
newsitem.headline: Gynecare says FDA panel to review therapy.

text.p: Gynecare Inc said on Monday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration will review its pre-market approval application for an investigational therapy for women with excessive menstrual bleeding.
The therapy, called the ThermaChoice Uterine Balloon Therapy system, will be reviewed on Oct 6 and 7, the company said in a statement. The application was submitted to the FDA on June 17, 1997.

ThermaChoice is intended to be a one-time, eight-minute treatment performed under local anesthesia. During the procedure, a balloon catheter is inserted vaginally into the uterus and inflated with sterile solution, which is then heated.
ThermaChoice is currently marketed internationally, and has been used to treat about 3,000 women, Gynecare said.
